findings.title: Null-safety fix applied to only one of four unguarded `modelSupplier.get()` calls
findings.description:
`getSubGroupsCount()` (lines 272-276) now guards against the delegate returning `null` when the group is deleted concurrently. The three paginated `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads directly above it (lines 256, 262, 268) still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` with no guard.

The same race is reachable through `GET /groups/{id}/children`: `GroupResource.getSubGroups` at `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupResource.java:180` calls `group.getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, -1, -1)` on a cached adapter.

Returning `Stream.empty()` when the model is `null` would match the "Never returns null" contract of those methods and the fallback pattern `CachedGroup` already uses via `DefaultLazyLoader`. The new test only lists top-level groups, so it does not cover this path.

findings.title: `getSubGroupsCount()` now returns `null`, contradicting the `GroupModel` contract
findings.description:
The Javadoc at `server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/GroupModel.java:294-298` states "Never returns {@code null}". The adapter now returns `null` for a concurrently deleted group.

The only caller today is `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` (`services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/GroupUtils.java:90`), which passes the value to `setSubGroupCount(Long)`, so nothing breaks at present. Any future caller that unboxes the result or does arithmetic on it will hit an NPE.

Either update the interface Javadoc to document `null` as "group no longer exists", or return `0L` to keep the contract. A side effect worth knowing: a group deleted mid-request is still returned in the listing, just with no `subGroupCount`.

findings.title: Reader thread is never joined and has no `finally`, so the test can miss failures and leak a spinning thread
findings.description:
Three related problems in `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`:

- **Missed failures:** the assertion at line 157 runs immediately after `deletedAll.set(true)` at line 155. The thread started at line 139 is never joined, so a list request still in flight (the one most likely to overlap the last deletes) can fail after the assertion has passed.
- **Leaked thread:** if any `remove()` at line 153 throws, `deletedAll` is never set. The non-daemon reader then loops forever, sending `max=Integer.MAX_VALUE` list requests at the shared server for the rest of the run. The delete loop needs `try { ... } finally { deletedAll.set(true); }` followed by a bounded `thread.join(timeout)` before asserting.
- **No proof of overlap:** nothing ensures the reader completed a single request during the delete window. A start latch or an assertion that at least one read happened would stop the test passing vacuously.

findings.title: Test groups are not registered for cleanup in the class-scoped realm
findings.description:
The 100 groups are created directly through `managedRealm.admin().groups().add(group)` and removed only by the test's own delete loop. `@InjectRealm` defaults to `LifeCycle.CLASS` (`test-framework/core/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testframework/annotations/InjectRealm.java:18`), so the realm is shared by every test in `GroupTest`.

If creation fails partway via `fail(...)` at line 131, or a delete throws, the remaining "Test Group N" groups stay in the realm and can affect later tests in the class. The project convention, visible in `AbstractGroupTest.createGroup` (`tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/AbstractGroupTest.java:57`), is `managedRealm.cleanup().add(r -> r.groups().group(groupId).remove())`. A cleanup hook would need to tolerate groups the test already deleted.

findings.title: Naming and style nits in the new test
findings.description:
- `groupUuuids` (lines 121, 129, 152) is a typo for `groupUuids`.
- Line 117 is a whitespace-only line, leaving a double blank before `@Test`; line 145 is a stray blank line inside the `catch` block.
- `Matchers.empty()` is used via a new non-static import (line 28), while the rest of the file uses static Hamcrest imports (lines 84-90).
- `Response.Status.Family.SUCCESSFUL` at line 126 could use the already imported `Status`.

findings.title: `@Override` added to `CachedGroup.getRealm()`
findings.description: `CachedGroup` implements `InRealm`, which declares `String getRealm()`, so the annotation is correct and adds compile-time checking.

findings.title: Removal of dead `groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement` from `GroupUtils`
findings.description: The removed private static method had no callers in `GroupUtils`. The only live use of that name is a separate three-argument private method in `server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/utils/ModelToRepresentation.java:209`. `StringUtil` has no remaining references under `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils`, so the removal leaves no unused import or broken reference.

findings.title: `getSubGroupsCount()` fix addresses the tested race
findings.description: The previous code dereferenced `getGroupModel()` directly, which returns `null` once another transaction has deleted the group. This was reached from `GroupsResource.getGroups` through `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount`. Switching to `modelSupplier.get()` with a null check removes that NPE and matches how the rest of the adapter obtains the delegate through `LazyModel`.
